//navigationFallback: The app routes on the client, so a cold load of /login must be answered with
index.html rather than a 404. The exclusions matter as much as the rule: without
them a mistyped asset path returns index.html with a 200, the browser tries to
parse HTML as JavaScript, and the failure surfaces far from its cause.

routes.//: Hashed filenames are content-addressed (outputHashing: all), so a year is safe — any change ships under a new name.
The entry document is the one file whose name never changes; caching it strands users on an old build.
Same reasoning — the bare route serves the same document.

//globalHeaders: connect-src names both back ends explicitly: the Managed Identity proxy (quotes)
and the Week-1 API (auth/login). Those are the only cross-origin destinations
this app may reach, so an injected script cannot exfiltrate anywhere else. Keep
style-src needs 'unsafe-inline' because the Angular build inlines critical CSS
into a <style> tag; script-src does not, because every script it emits is a file.

globalHeaders.content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://day17-mi-proxy.bluesky-eec20d45.centralindia.azurecontainerapps.io https://day-5-piece-2.bluesky-eec20d45.centralindia.azurecontainerapps.io; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'

//platform: No apiRuntime block: this Static Web App has no managed functions. The Managed Identity lives on a separate Container App (mi-proxy/), because SWA's managed functions cannot be given one on the Free plan.
